name: CA-23
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Obernolte has a large financial advantage
Markets price Obernolte at ~93% to win
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The district's Republican lean, Obernolte's incumbency and roughly 18-to-1 cash advantage, and prediction markets pricing him near 93% all point to a comfortable Republican win. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpectedly competitive top-two dynamic could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jay Obernolte, the Republican incumbent, seeks re-election in a California district that leans Republican by about nine points. He advanced to the general election and faces Democrat Tessa Lynn Hodge, a first-time challenger with minimal fundraising. Obernolte has raised about $1.5 million and holds over $1.6 million in cash, dwarfing Hodge's roughly $80,000 raised and $10,000 on hand. Outside spending has been modest and mostly favors the incumbent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and money, all of which favor Obernolte. Prediction markets give him roughly a 93% chance of winning. The race is rated Likely Republican, with Hodge needing a major shift in the environment or resources to be competitive.
